theater: 尼羅河三角洲西部大河大彎

battle.name: 利比亞戰役
battle.theater: 尼羅河三角洲西部大河大彎
battle.brief: 公元前1250年前後，法老梅內普塔在尼羅河三角洲西部迎擊梅什韋什人與海上民族聯軍。利比亞首領梅雷亞什率部眾與車馬壓境，法老先遣梅德亞伊步兵與弓箭手在大河大彎截住先鋒，再以主力師與戰車合圍。埃及長矛在縱隊前排待命，專戳馬腿、斷挽具。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 利比亞戰役是埃及新王國第十九王朝法老梅內普塔在位第五年迎戰西部沙漠梅什韋什人聯盟的一役，交戰的兩邊沒有共同的文字、曆法與制度，聯盟只在戰場上短暫重合。埃及方面以法老本人為最高統帥，軍中分為數個步兵師，每師由王子或資深軍官分領，另有獨立的弓箭手大隊、常駐三角洲西部與沙漠邊緣的梅德亞伊邊防步兵，以及由御林軍簇衛的戰車部隊；後勤靠尼羅河船運與驢隊維持，這場戰役中攻城器械完全沒有使用。利比亞方面是西部沙海諸部落的聯盟：梅什韋什人自「荷魯斯之山」以西的綠洲路線與牧道南下，由首領梅雷亞什率領，馬匹與輕型車輛同行；同一時期出現在三角洲北岸的還有來自地中海的海上民族，卡納克銘文與梅內普塔石碑留下謝爾登、謝克萊什、厄克威什、泰雷什、盧卡等名號。外圍局勢是赫梯王國正經歷王位交接，埃及與赫梯以白銀為憑的和約在戰役同年重新確認，法老因此把西境戰事放在整體外交格局裡經營，而不是單純的邊境掃蕩。
countriesEn: The Battle of Libya was fought in the fifth regnal year of Merneptah, pharaoh of the New Kingdom of Egypt and of the Nineteenth Dynasty, against a coalition of Meshwesh (Libyan) peoples from the western desert. The two sides shared no script, no calendar and no institutions; their alliance lasted only as long as the battlefield. On the Egyptian side the pharaoh himself was supreme commander. The host was divided into several infantry divisions, each led by a prince or a senior officer, with a separate body of archers, the Medjay frontier infantry who garrisoned the western Delta and the desert margin, and a chariot corps screened by the royal guard. Supply was carried on Nile shipping and by donkey trains, and no siege works were used in this campaign at all. The Libyan side was a confederation of tribes from the desert sands: the Meshwesh came south along the oasis routes and the caravan tracks west of the Mountains of Horus under their chief Meryeyash, with horses and light vehicles moving with them. At the same time peoples from the Mediterranean appeared along the northern coast of the Delta, the Karnak inscription and the Merneptah Stele preserving the names Sherden, Shekelesh, Ekwesh, Teresh and Lukka. The wider situation was a Hittite kingdom in the middle of a royal succession, and the silver treaty between Egypt and Hatti was reconfirmed in the very year of the battle, so the pharaoh was running the western front as part of a whole diplomatic settlement rather than a routine frontier sweep.
people: 關鍵人物中，站在埃及一方的核心是法老梅內普塔，也就是拉美西斯二世的第三子、第十九王朝的第四位法老；他有用刻碑記功的習慣，把整場戰役完整地留在石頭上，後世才得以知道敵方首領的名字。他的長子阿蒙赫爾赫佩謝夫隨軍出征，率一支部隊掩護前鋒，卻在西部沙漠的佩爾－德胡提綠洲一帶病逝，遺體運回底比斯安葬，埃及博物館現藏其石棺。梅雷亞什是利比亞方面的首領，率領大批部眾、車馬越過沙海進逼三角洲，後來在「大河大彎」被埃及軍隊分割包圍，部眾潰散後往西逃走。埃及將領中還有掌管弓箭手大隊與梅德亞伊步兵的高階軍官，以及率領戰車部隊的御林軍將官；卡納克銘文以「王的眾子」統稱隨征的王族成員，並記下王子所部全程不離法老左右。海上民族方面沒有留下可考的指揮者姓名，碑銘只記部族名號與俘獲數字，而後世史家正是靠這些殘缺的人名，才把這場戰役與隨後百餘年間地中海東岸的連續崩潰連成一線。
peopleEn: The central figure on the Egyptian side was the pharaoh Merneptah himself, the third son of Ramesses II and the fourth king of the Nineteenth Dynasty. He was a ruler with a habit of monumental self-documenting, and he carved the whole campaign into stone, which is how later generations learned the name of the enemy commander. His eldest son Amenherkhepeshef marched with the army and led a detachment screening the vanguard, but fell ill and died in the western desert around the oasis of Per-Djehuty; his body was brought back to Thebes for burial, and his sarcophagus is kept today in the Egyptian Museum. Meryeyash was the chief on the Libyan side, leading a large body of men, horses and vehicles out of the sands toward the Delta, only to be split up and surrounded by the Egyptian force at the Great Bend, with the survivors fleeing west. On the Egyptian staff were the senior officers who commanded the body of archers and the Medjay infantry, together with the commander of the chariot corps and the officers of the royal guard; the Karnak inscription refers collectively to the king's sons as accompanying him and records that the princes' troops never left the king. Among the sea peoples no commander's name has survived: the monuments give only the names of the tribes and the tally of captives. It was from these fragmentary names that later historians stitched this battle into the long chain of collapses along the eastern Mediterranean in the centuries that followed.
kits: 卡面這支埃及長矛，是新王國步兵最基本也最耐用的冷兵器：銅或青銅鑄成的柳葉形矛頭，以繩索綁在木杆上，全長約兩公尺，握處常留一段纏繩防滑。卡納克壁畫顯示它常置於縱隊前排，長矛手排成密集橫線，後方才是弓箭手，最後是預備隊；面對來自西方或北方的車陣時，矛手的任務不是刺人，而是壓低矛尖去戳馬腿、割斷挽具與韁繩，把敵方戰車逼停，再由弓箭手與持斧兵上前收拾。新王國步兵通常還配備複合弓與箭、科普什鉤形砍刀、扇刃戰斧與短標槍；防護是皮或麻布製的方牌與圓盾，約一米口徑，內襯皮革，箭袋斜掛於腰背。戰車是雙人雙馬、六根車輻的木製輕車，車上一名御者、一名戰士，後者持矛與鉤刀；拉美西斯二世時期王室與盟軍合計的戰車以數千輛計。利比亞人則帶著弓、矛、小圓盾與短刀，並且自備馬匹與輕車，顯示這批沙漠部眾並非純粹的步行游群。運輸方面沒有車隊而靠驢隊與河船，攻城器在本役中完全缺席。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on this card was the most basic and most durable cold weapon of the New Kingdom infantry. A copper or bronze leaf-shaped head was bound to a wooden shaft with cord, the whole about two metres long, with a short wrap of cord at the grip to stop it slipping in wet or bloodied hands. The Karnak paintings show it carried in the front ranks of the column: the spearmen stood in a dense line, the archers behind them, the reserves at the rear. Facing a war-wagon formation coming out of the west or the north, the job of the spearmen was not to kill men but to lower the point into the legs of the horses, cut through the traces and reins, stop the enemy chariots dead, and leave them to be finished off by the archers and the axe-men. New Kingdom infantry also carried composite bows and arrows, the khopesh sickle-sword, the fan-bladed axe and short javelins; protection was a rectangular or round shield of leather or linen, roughly a metre across and lined with hide, with the quiver slung at the back. The chariot was a light two-man, two-horse vehicle with six spokes, one driver and one warrior, the latter armed with spear and khopesh; under Ramesses II the royal and allied chariot corps together ran into the thousands. The Libyans came with bows, spears, small round shields and short swords, and they brought their own horses and light wagons, which shows that these desert hosts were not purely foot infantry. On the logistics side there were no wagon trains at all, only donkey trains and river boats, and siege engines were entirely absent from this campaign.
tactics: 埃及軍的部署是分三次出擊的縱深結構。第一波由梅德亞伊步兵與弓箭手大隊組成，輕裝急行，先去截住利比亞先鋒，目的是在大河大彎以東的路段把敵人拖住，不讓其接觸三角洲的耕地與城鎮。第二波是主力步兵師，與法老及王的眾子同行，沿河谷與堤道行軍，在水源充足的地區展開，因為沙漠路只能維持有限時間的給養，而河運能持續供應穀物、銅料與箭杆。第三波是戰車部隊與弓箭手，負責封住往西與往北的退路，並在敵營被擊潰時追擊散兵。作戰多在清晨與黃昏發動，靠突然襲擊與密集矢雨壓制敵陣，再以矛線推進與車陣衝撞合圍；銘文自述王的眾子所部全程貼身近衛。整場戰役還有一條糧道上的關鍵：一旦利比亞聯軍佔領西緣牧地與綠洲水源，埃及就有可能被迫放棄部分牧場與商路，這也是法老在農業收成季節仍要遠征的理由。
tacticsEn: The Egyptian deployment was a deep structure fought in three waves. The first was formed from Medjay infantry and the body of archers, moving light and fast in order to intercept the Libyan vanguard; the object was to hold the enemy on the approaches east of the Great Bend and not let them reach the fields and towns of the Delta. The second was the main infantry divisions marching with the pharaoh and with the king's sons, moving along the river valley and the embankment roads and deploying where water was plentiful, because the desert track can support supply for only a limited time while river transport can carry grain, copper and arrow-shafts continuously. The third was the chariot corps and the archers, who closed the roads west and north and pursued the broken enemy once the camp had been overrun. Fighting was opened in the early morning and at dusk, relying on surprise and dense arrow fall to break the enemy order, then advancing the spear line and closing with a chariot charge; the inscription states that the troops of the king's sons stayed in close attendance on the king throughout. A further key point lay in the supply route: if the Libyan coalition seized the grazing lands and the oasis water on the western margin, Egypt might be forced to give up part of its pastures and caravan trade. That is why the pharaoh campaigned at all in the season of the agricultural harvest.
data: 關於數字，史料能給的極有限，而且大多出自法老自己的宣傳碑文。梅內普塔石碑（又稱以色列石碑）高約三公尺，碑面有二十七行聖書體，記錄的戰果是俘虜九千三百七十六人、馬匹六千三百五十九匹；卡納克大殿的第五年戰記銘文則補充了王族、弓箭手與梅德亞伊部隊參戰的過程。這些數字是王室自述，學界一般視為誇張的戰果宣傳，真實俘虜數應低於此，但仍可判斷敵方投入的兵力是以萬計的量級。年代上，卡片所標的公元前1250年是一個寬鬆的下限，學界一般依梅內普塔在位第五年推算該役約在公元前1208年，登基年一般定於公元前1213年、退位於公元前1203年，戰役落在埃及曆沙姆月第三月，即約四月至五月，選在收穫之後而沙漠通道仍可通行之際。地理上，底比斯到「大河大彎」前線約六百公里上下，軍隊靠河船與驢隊完成補給。戰車數量沒有留下可靠記載，只能依新王國鼎盛期的規模推想為數百至數千輛之間。
dataEn: On numbers the evidence is extremely thin, and most of it comes from the pharaoh's own victory inscriptions. The Merneptah Stele, also called the Israel Stele, stands about three metres high and carries twenty-seven lines of hieroglyphs; it claims nine thousand three hundred and seventy-six prisoners and six thousand three hundred and fifty-nine horses taken. The year-five battle inscription in the Great Karnak hypostyle hall adds the part played by the royal princes, the archers and the Medjay troops. These figures are the royal party's own account, and scholars generally treat them as exaggerated triumphal reporting; the real number of prisoners must have been lower, but the order of magnitude of the enemy force, thousands upon thousands, is clear. As for dating, the year 1250 BCE carried on this card is a loose lower bound: scholars place the campaign in Merneptah's fifth year, generally computed as around 1208 BCE, with his accession dated to 1213 BCE and his death to 1203 BCE; the campaign fell in the third month of Shemu, roughly April to May, chosen for a time after the harvest but while the desert tracks were still passable. Geographically the front at the Great Bend lay some six hundred kilometres from Thebes, and the army was supplied by river boats and donkey trains. No reliable figure survives for the number of chariots; one can only infer from the scale of the New Kingdom at its height that it lay somewhere between several hundred and several thousand.
cause: 打起來的原因有多層。最直接的是西部沙漠的壓力：梅什韋什人從「荷魯斯之山」以西的沙地與綠洲地帶南下，在尼羅河三角洲西緣游牧與劫掠，這種壓力自中王朝起便周期性出現，到拉美西斯二世晚年更因亞洲與近東同時動盪而加劇。經濟層面上，埃及的西部商路、綠洲貿易與牧場是法老收稅與調兵的對象，敵人推進就等於切斷收入與軍馬來源。與之同步的是地中海東岸的連續遷移：謝爾登、謝克萊什等海上部族沿黎凡特海岸向北移動，在三角洲北岸尋找登陸與掠奪的據點，與利比亞人形成南北夾擊的格局。此外，梅內普塔即位時的新王國已遠離拉美西斯二世的全盛，戰車與兵員編制都在收縮，國庫吃緊，繼承人年幼，需要一場乾淨的邊境勝利來穩住軍心與朝局，這也是他事後大量刻碑的原因。
causeEn: There were several layers of cause. The most immediate was pressure from the western desert: the Meshwesh came down out of the sands and oases west of the Mountains of Horus, pasturing and raiding along the western margin of the Nile Delta. Such pressure had recurred periodically since the Middle Kingdom, and by the late years of Ramesses II it had sharpened as Asia and the Near East moved at the same time. On the economic level the western caravan routes, the oasis trade and the pastures of Egypt were taxable and supplied the pharaoh's troops and horses, so an enemy advance meant lost revenue and lost remounts. Running in step with it was the successive movement of peoples along the eastern Mediterranean coast: the Sherden, the Shekelesh and their companions moved north along the Levantine shore, seeking landing places and plunder on the northern coast of the Delta, so that the Libyans and the sea peoples closed on Egypt from north and south together. On top of this, the New Kingdom Merneptah inherited was far from the high point of Ramesses II: the chariot and man-power establishment was contracting, the treasury was strained and the heir was a boy. He needed one clean frontier victory to steady the army and the court, and that is also why he carved so much stone afterwards.
impact: 這一役的直接影響，是把西部邊疆推回梅什韋什人的勢力圈之外。埃及得以重新控制「大河大彎」一帶的牧地與通行權，把梅德亞伊邊防軍與一批新附庸的西部部族編入三角洲防衛體系，之後百餘年間埃及在西線的威懾力一直維持到拉美西斯三世的時代，梅什韋什人再未以大規模聯盟的形式越過沙漠。政治上，這場勝利讓梅內普塔取得一筆難得的資本，在他死後的權力轉移中，擁護者仍能援引「西境大捷」為合法性背書，也讓他得以把大量戰俘編入王室土地與軍隊，補充因常年徵召而空缺的勞動力。長期來看，它同時是一次警號：海上民族並未因一役而退，公元前十二世紀整整一百年，東地中海沿岸不斷出現新的部族聯盟，埃及靠尼羅河的地理屏障與制度韌性撐了過去，而同一時期的赫梯王國卻在此起彼伏的攻擊中崩潰。再者，這批銘文成為後世重建該時期的關鍵文本，同時具備王權宣傳、法律文本與戰爭實錄三重價值。
impactEn: The immediate effect of the battle was to push the western frontier back beyond the sphere of Meshwesh power. Egypt recovered control of the pastures and the lines of movement around the Great Bend, and folded the Medjay frontier troops and a batch of newly attached western tribes into the defence of the Delta; for more than a century afterwards the deterrent effect of Egypt in the west held firm into the reign of Ramesses III, and the Meshwesh never again crossed the desert as a great coalition. Politically the victory gave Merneptah a rare capital that his supporters could still invoke as the legitimating deed of the reign after his death, and it allowed him to enrol large numbers of prisoners on royal estates and in the army, filling the labour gap left by constant conscription. In the longer run the victory was also a warning: the sea peoples did not withdraw after one battle, and for a full century of the twelfth century BCE new tribal coalitions kept forming along the eastern Mediterranean. Egypt survived them on the strength of the Nile's geographical barrier and the resilience of its institutions, whereas the Hittite kingdom, attacked from several quarters at once, collapsed. The inscriptions themselves became the key texts by which the period is reconstructed, carrying at once the value of royal propaganda, of a legal document and of a battlefield record.
result: 結果是埃及在戰役中取勝，但取勝的範圍與代價都被銘文誇大了。梅雷亞什率領的利比亞主力在「大河大彎」被擊潰，部眾被分割包圍，殘部向西潰散，據碑文自述共俘虜九千三百七十六人、馬六千三百五十九匹；同時出現在北岸的海上民族被逐回海上方向，此後再沒有以整軍聯盟的方式大舉進入三角洲。埃及軍的損失沒有被記錄，長子阿蒙赫爾赫佩謝夫在戰役期間病逝，使這場勝利帶上私人代價；軍隊返程時還必然面臨戰俘與牲口的分配、以及編入軍隊與莊園的處置問題。戰役結束後，法老把成果刻上卡納克牆壁與石碑，宣布與赫梯的和約重新生效並把相關內容附在同一塊碑上，「以色列」一名號因此在聖書體銘文中首次出現，成為聖經以外最古老的相關記載。此役並未改變地中海東岸的整體走向：近十年後梅內普塔去世，他的兒子西普塔赫短命而終，塞提二世與其子埃門梅塞相繼爭位，帝國在接下來半個世紀裡才真正經歷王朝更替與外敵環伺的雙重擠壓。
resultEn: The result was an Egyptian victory, though both the reach of that victory and its cost are exaggerated by the monuments. Meryeyash's Libyan main force was broken at the Great Bend: the host was split up and surrounded, the survivors scattered west, and the inscriptions claim nine thousand three hundred and seventy-six prisoners and six thousand three hundred and fifty-nine horses. The sea peoples who had appeared on the northern coast were driven back seaward, and afterwards they never entered the Delta again in any strength as an organised coalition. Egyptian losses are not recorded, and the death from illness of the king's eldest son Amenherkhepeshef during the campaign gave the victory a private cost. On the march home the army also had to settle the distribution of prisoners and livestock and the question of how the captives were to be absorbed into the army and onto estates. When the fighting was over the pharaoh carved the results on the Karnak walls and on the stele, announced the reaffirmation of the treaty with Hatti, and attached the terms to the same monument; the name Israel thereby appears for the first time in a hieroglyphic inscription, and it is the oldest such reference outside the Bible. The campaign did not change the general direction of the eastern Mediterranean. Some ten years later Merneptah died, his son Siptah reigned only briefly, Seti II and his son Amenmesse then contested the throne, and only in the following half century did the empire face the double pressure of dynastic turnover and enemies on every side.
